title: Prove uniform Gaussian boundary conditioning at the production scale
body:
The retained full-cell Gaussian boundary theorem holds only for fixed alpha, so it does not justify the source's production choice `alpha=ceil(sqrt((4/pi)log(16p)))`. This package proves a uniform relative two-edge operator limit for `theta^(1/10) <= b=pi/alpha² <= 1`, which contains the actual production scale and its complete theta interval eventually. Normalized q-product ratios remove the previous absolute constants. A corollary gives `||K^-1||₂ <= p^(2+eta)` eventually for every fixed positive eta, preserving the source's ceiling, floor, phase and complete infinite-product coefficient.

The exact untruncated full cell is the scope. This does not admit a capped RawGaussian program, rounded reference, inverse algorithm, physical execution or new kappa. Preparation, truncation, precision, storage, movement and outer recovery remain explicit obligations.

Validation: normal and optimized registered checks; 98 exact elimination comparisons, 7,906 original-source geometry pairs, 216 rescaled exponent comparisons, nonvacuous rational product enclosures and falsifying controls; committed-byte/source-history preflight; official export integrity; isolated Git-free normal/optimized replay; source and receipt mutation rejection. The uniform statement is the written proof, not extrapolation from these finite checks.

Canonical claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4202#discussioncomment-19172868

Credit the retained Jose Manuel/#4193, Vlado Vojdanovski/#1673, Cinna Davis/PR4100, Ryanson Jonathan/#4435, Nick Petalas/#5150 and JoyboyBrian boundary-limit lineage, together with the classical q-LDU and product identities.
